notes:
Inbound SMB lead via self-serve signup (trial credits used). Main ask: move chat assistant into prod but seeing unpredictable latency from hosted API. Customer is lightweight e-comm checkout assistant (product recommendations + short Q&A).

Summary of constraints / ask:
- Primary region: us-east (customer hosted frontend in us-east-1). Seeing 200-800ms token latency, occasional spikes >1.2s. Target: sub-300ms median generation for short prompts.
- Throughput: low concurrent (5-20 rps peak), latency-sensitive. Cost conscious.
- Wants guidance on region choice, timeouts, and prompt-length best practices to improve tail latencies.
- Prefers public cloud (no VPC/on-prem). SOC2 required for pilot logs retention. SSO later.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-02-25: Self-serve signup, trial started. AE Maya assigned automatically.
- 2026-02-27: First email from dev lead (attached thread). Reports "latency inconsistent after midday traffic".
- 2026-03-01: 15m discovery call (ff_20260301_qk01). Developer walked through SDK usage; they call gpt-like endpoint with ~120 token prompts + 60 token completion.
- 2026-03-02: SE (Arjun) did quick trace — found calls from us-east hitting hosted API region auto-route to us-west occasionally due to nearest-pop routing fallback. Noted socket timeout defaults at 60s but client-side request retries set aggressively causing queuing at runtime.
- 2026-03-03: Sent configuration checklist: switch to region-explicit endpoint, increase streaming chunk size, lower client retry backoff. Customer ran small A/B and reported improved med latency (~270ms) but tail still high.
- 2026-03-04: Customer ran generation with longer context (system + history ~400 tokens) and saw 800-1200ms waits; concerns about prompt length and model selection.

Notes from devs/quotes:
- "We love the simplicity but tail latency kills UX around 2pm–5pm." — Emma (CTO).
- "Our stack can't tolerate consistent >500ms per turn for chat." — Raj (Lead Eng).

SE observations and quick wins suggested:
- Region choice: pin requests to us-east-1 explicit host to avoid cross-region routing; run simple synthetic test to measure p50/p95 across us-east-1 vs us-west-2.
- Timeouts: set client-side socket timeout to 10s, but reduce retry attempts for GET/generate to avoid queue amplification (1 retry max, exponential backoff).
- Streaming: enable streaming responses to render partial tokens earlier; use smaller initial chunk to get first tokens to user quickly.
- Prompt engineering: limit system + context to <300 tokens for interactive assistant; offload long docs to embeddings + retrieval for doc search.
- Model & config: recommend using a lower-latency variant or shorter-context model for chat (if available in our catalog). Try response_length cap and temperature to reduce sampling time.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated prompts (welcome message) and KV cache reuse for conversational turns recommended.

Open questions / blockers:
- Customer wants SLA numbers for hosted p95 in us-east for small workloads. Need to provide empirical latency profiles or perf-run.
- Cost sensitivity: they want tradeoffs (quantized model vs higher latency).

Next steps (action owner):
- Maya: schedule 30m POC kickoff with Emma + Raj + Arjun (target 2026-03-08).
- Arjun: prepare perf checklist and run 3-day synthetic p50/p95 across regions (deliver by 2026-03-07).
- Devs: test region-pinned endpoint and streaming change; report p50/p95 and UX screenshots.

Jira / support: INF-11258 opened to track observed latency spikes and investigational traces. Drive: POC_Perf_Checklist_2026-03-02.pdf (templated). Gmail thread contains initial logs.

Short-term ask from customer: "Can Redwood recommend exact client-timeout settings + region endpoint to hit sub-300ms med for short chat turns?" — they want quick config they can flip in prod if POC ok.

CRM style next step: POC kickoff -> run region test -> share perf report -> agree pilot SLA + small reserved monthly commit (if results good).
